#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Measure real upstream cache usage during consecutive Codex turns, without logging prompts/keys."""
import argparse
import hashlib
import http.server
import json
from pathlib import Path
import socket
import subprocess
import tempfile
import threading
import time
import tomllib
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
import yaml

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--model", default="a0-qwen")
parser.add_argument("--config", type=Path, default=Path.home() / ".config/codex-bridge/config.yaml")
parser.add_argument("--report", type=Path)
args = parser.parse_args()
source = args.config.read_text()
config = tomllib.loads(source) if args.config.suffix == ".toml" else yaml.safe_load(source)
model = next(m for m in config["models"] if m["name"] == args.model)
assert model["api"] == "chat", "This test measures the Chat Completions adapter."
upstream = model["base_url"].rstrip("/")
records = []


class NoRedirect(urllib.request.HTTPRedirectHandler):
    def redirect_request(self, req, fp, code, msg, headers, newurl):
        return None


class Tap(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, *_):
        pass

    def do_POST(self):
        raw = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"]))
        record = {"body": json.loads(raw), "usage": None}
        records.append(record)
        endpoint = upstream if upstream.endswith("/chat/completions") else upstream + "/chat/completions"
        request = urllib.request.Request(endpoint, data=raw, headers={
            "Authorization": [REDACTED]"Authorization", ""),
            "Content-Type": "application/json", "Accept": "text/event-stream"})
        try:
            with urllib.request.build_opener(NoRedirect).open(request, timeout=150) as response:
                self.send_response(response.status)
                self.send_header("Content-Type", response.headers["Content-Type"])
                self.end_headers()
                pending = b""
                while chunk := response.read1(65536):
                    pending += chunk
                    while b"\n" in pending:
                        line, pending = pending.split(b"\n", 1)
                        if line.startswith(b"data:") and line[5:].strip() != b"[DONE]":
                            payload = json.loads(line[5:])
                            if payload.get("usage"):
                                record["usage"] = payload["usage"]
                    self.wfile.write(chunk)
                    self.wfile.flush()
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
            self.send_response(error.code)
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(error.read())


def fingerprint(value):
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()).hexdigest()


with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="bridge-cache-") as directory:
    root = Path(directory)
    work = root / "work"
    work.mkdir()
    tap = http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Tap)
    threading.Thread(target=tap.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
    with socket.socket() as listener:
        listener.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        port = listener.getsockname()[1]
    config["listen"] = f"127.0.0.1:{port}"
    for entry in config["models"]:
        entry["base_url"] = f"http://127.0.0.1:{tap.server_port}/v1"
    private_path = root / "config.yaml"
    private_path.write_text(yaml.safe_dump(config, sort_keys=False))
    private_path.chmod(0o600)
    with (root / "proxy.log").open("w") as log:
        process = subprocess.Popen(["codex-bridge", "--config", str(private_path), "serve"], stdout=log, stderr=log)
    report = {"model": args.model, "turns": []}
    try:
        for _ in range(100):
            try:
                token = (root / "config.yaml.token").read_text()
                health = urllib.request.Request(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/health", headers={"X-Codex-Bridge-Token": token})
                with urllib.request.urlopen(health, timeout=1):
                    break
            except (OSError, urllib.error.URLError):
                assert process.poll() is None, (root / "proxy.log").read_text()
                time.sleep(0.1)
        else:
            raise AssertionError("test bridge did not start")
        overrides = ["-c", 'model_provider="codex-bridge"',
                     "-c", f'model_providers.codex-bridge.base_url="http://127.0.0.1:{port}/v1"',
                     "-c", f'model_providers.codex-bridge.http_headers.X-Codex-Bridge-Token="{token}"',
                     "-c", "model_providers.codex-bridge.requires_openai_auth=false"]
        thread = None
        previous_usage = {}
        for turn in range(1, 5):
            before = len(records)
            command = ["codex", "exec"] + (["resume", thread] if thread else [])
            command += ["--skip-git-repo-check", "-m", args.model, "--json"] + overrides
            prompt = f"Cache verification turn {turn}. Reply exactly ACK-{turn}. Do not use any tools."
            if turn == 1:
                reference = "\n".join(f"Reference row {i:04d}: amber cobalt delta evergreen." for i in range(150))
                prompt = "Keep this reference unchanged for later turns:\n" + reference + "\n" + prompt
            result = subprocess.run(command + ["--", prompt], cwd=work, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=180)
            assert result.returncode == 0, result.stdout + result.stderr
            events = [json.loads(line) for line in result.stdout.splitlines()]
            current_thread = next(e["thread_id"] for e in events if e["type"] == "thread.started")
            assert thread is None or current_thread == thread
            thread = current_thread
            codex_usage = next(e["usage"] for e in events if e["type"] == "turn.completed")
            new = records[before:]
            assert new and all(r["usage"] for r in new), "upstream omitted usage"
            requests = []
            for index, record in enumerate(new, start=before):
                usage, body = record["usage"], record["body"]
                assert body.get("prompt_cache_key"), "Codex cache key was lost"
                inputs = usage["prompt_tokens"]
                cached = usage.get("prompt_tokens_details", {}).get("cached_tokens", usage.get("prompt_cache_hit_tokens", 0))
                assert 0 <= cached <= inputs
                row = {"input_tokens": inputs, "cached_input_tokens": cached,
                       "uncached_input_tokens": inputs - cached, "hit_ratio": cached / inputs,
                       "upstream_usage": usage}
                if index:
                    prior = records[index - 1]["body"]
                    row["cache_key_stable"] = body.get("prompt_cache_key") == prior.get("prompt_cache_key")
                    row["tools_stable"] = fingerprint(body.get("tools")) == fingerprint(prior.get("tools"))
                    row["prior_messages_unchanged"] = prior["messages"] == body["messages"][:len(prior["messages"])]
                    assert all(row[k] for k in ("cache_key_stable", "tools_stable", "prior_messages_unchanged")), row
                requests.append(row)
            raw_input = sum(r["input_tokens"] for r in requests)
            raw_cached = sum(r["cached_input_tokens"] for r in requests)
            # Codex resume reports cumulative thread usage; compare each turn's delta.
            delta = {key: codex_usage[key] - previous_usage.get(key, 0)
                     for key in ("input_tokens", "cached_input_tokens", "output_tokens")}
            assert delta == {"input_tokens": raw_input, "cached_input_tokens": raw_cached,
                             "output_tokens": sum(r["upstream_usage"]["completion_tokens"] for r in requests)}, delta
            previous_usage = codex_usage
            report["turns"].append({"turn": turn, "requests": requests, "codex_usage": codex_usage,
                                    "codex_usage_delta": delta})
            print(f"{args.model} turn {turn}: input={raw_input}, cached={raw_cached}, uncached={raw_input-raw_cached}, hit={raw_cached/raw_input:.2%}; stable_prefix={turn == 1 or requests[0]['prior_messages_unchanged']}", flush=True)
            # The provider may publish cache entries asynchronously.
            time.sleep(2)
        warm = [r for turn in report["turns"][1:] for r in turn["requests"]]
        report["subsequent_turns_weighted_hit_ratio"] = sum(r["cached_input_tokens"] for r in warm) / sum(r["input_tokens"] for r in warm)
        assert any(r["cached_input_tokens"] > 0 for r in warm), "provider reported no subsequent cache hits; inspect report"
        report["thread_id"] = thread
        if args.report:
            args.report.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")
        print(f"PASS stable prompt prefix and exact usage accounting; subsequent weighted hit ratio {report['subsequent_turns_weighted_hit_ratio']:.2%}", flush=True)
    finally:
        process.terminate()
        process.wait(timeout=15)
        tap.shutdown()
        tap.server_close()

name: Build and release codex-bridge

on:
  push:
    branches: ['**']
    tags: ['v*']

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: codex-bridge-${{ github.ref_type == 'tag' && 'release' || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  TAG: ${{ github.ref_type == 'tag' && github.ref_name || github.sha }}

jobs:
  build:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: linux
            arch: amd64
            runner: ubuntu-24.04
          - os: linux
            arch: arm64
            runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
          - os: darwin
            arch: arm64
            runner: macos-15
          - os: darwin
            arch: amd64
            runner: macos-15-intel
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
      - name: Validate release tag
        if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
        run: python3 .github/release-notes.py "$TAG" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-notes.md"
      - name: Verify
        run: |
          python3 .github/release-notes.py --self-test
          go test -race ./...
          go vet ./...
      - name: Build and check native binary
        env:
          OS: ${{ matrix.os }}
          ARCH: ${{ matrix.arch }}
        run: |
          test "$(go env GOOS)" = "$OS"
          test "$(go env GOARCH)" = "$ARCH"
          mkdir -p release
          binary="release/codex-bridge-$OS-$ARCH"
          CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS="$OS" GOARCH="$ARCH" go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w -X main.version=$TAG" -o "$binary" .
          "$binary" --help
          test "$(env -u HOME -u XDG_CONFIG_HOME "$binary" --version)" = "codex-bridge $TAG"
          if "$binary" --config "$RUNNER_TEMP/uninitialized.yaml" status > "$RUNNER_TEMP/status.txt" 2>/dev/null; then
            exit 1
          fi
          grep -Fx "Version: $TAG" "$RUNNER_TEMP/status.txt"
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        if: matrix.os == 'darwin'
        with:
          node-version: '22'
      - name: Native macOS lifecycle and Codex checks
        if: matrix.os == 'darwin'
        env:
          ARCH: ${{ matrix.arch }}
        run: |
          sw_vers
          uname -m
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/codex" @openai/codex@0.164.0
          python3 tests/picker.py --codex "$RUNNER_TEMP/codex/node_modules/.bin/codex" --bridge "$PWD/release/codex-bridge-darwin-$ARCH"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: binary-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
          path: release/*
          if-no-files-found: error

  publish:
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: binary-*
          path: release
          merge-multiple: true
      - name: Prepare release assets and notes
        run: |
          test -f release/codex-bridge-linux-amd64
          test -f release/codex-bridge-linux-arm64
          test -f release/codex-bridge-darwin-amd64
          test -f release/codex-bridge-darwin-arm64
          cp LICENSE THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md release/
          (cd release && sha256sum codex-bridge-* > checksums.txt)
          python3 .github/release-notes.py "$TAG" > release-notes.md
      - name: Prepare draft
        id: release
        uses: actions/github-script@v8
        with:
          script: |
            const fs = require('fs');
            const {owner, repo} = context.repo;
            const tag = process.env.TAG;
            const version = s => {
              if (!/^v(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$/.test(s)) throw new Error('Invalid stable tag');
              return s.slice(1).split('.').map(BigInt);
            };
            let latest = true;
            try {
              const current = version((await github.rest.repos.getLatestRelease({owner, repo})).data.tag_name);
              const next = version(tag);
              latest = next.some((n, i) => n > current[i] && next.slice(0, i).every((v, j) => v === current[j]));
            } catch (error) { if (error.status !== 404) throw error; }
            let release;
            try {
              release = (await github.rest.repos.getReleaseByTag({owner, repo, tag})).data;
              if (!release.draft) throw new Error('Refusing to overwrite a published release');
            } catch (error) {
              if (error.status !== 404) throw error;
              release = (await github.rest.repos.createRelease({
                owner, repo, tag_name: tag, name: `codex-bridge ${tag}`, draft: true,
                body: fs.readFileSync('release-notes.md', 'utf8')
              })).data;
            }
            core.setOutput('id', release.id);
            core.setOutput('latest', String(latest));
      - name: Upload verified release assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: gh release upload "$TAG" release/* --clobber
      - name: Publish complete GitHub release
        uses: actions/github-script@v8
        env:
          RELEASE_ID: ${{ steps.release.outputs.id }}
          MAKE_LATEST: ${{ steps.release.outputs.latest }}
        with:
          script: |
            await github.rest.repos.updateRelease({
              ...context.repo, release_id: Number(process.env.RELEASE_ID),
              draft: false, make_latest: process.env.MAKE_LATEST
            });

# codex-bridge - Use external models alongside your ChatGPT subscription in Codex CLI - Configure any chat completions endpoint and model and merge with Codex model list - Change models on the fly with `/model` selector ![Codex model picker showing external models alongside OpenAI subscription models](.github/assets/model-picker.webp) ## Quick guide ```sh # Edit the models config codex-bridge edit # Start the proxy service codex-bridge start # Sync models (--force restarts the Codex server) codex-bridge sync --force # Start Codex as usual and choose a model with /model codex ``` ## Install ### Linux **x86_64 / amd64** ```sh curl -fL https://github.com/agent0ai/codex-bridge/releases/latest/download/codex-bridge-linux-amd64 -o codex-bridge-linux-amd64 && mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin" && install -m 755 codex-bridge-linux-amd64 "$HOME/.local/bin/codex-bridge" ``` **ARM64 / aarch64** ```sh curl -fL https://github.com/agent0ai/codex-bridge/releases/latest/download/codex-bridge-linux-arm64 -o codex-bridge-linux-arm64 && mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin" && install -m 755 codex-bridge-linux-arm64 "$HOME/.local/bin/codex-bridge" ``` ### macOS **Apple Silicon / arm64** ```sh curl -fL https://github.com/agent0ai/codex-bridge/releases/latest/download/codex-bridge-darwin-arm64 -o codex-bridge-darwin-arm64 && mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin" && install -m 755 codex-bridge-darwin-arm64 "$HOME/.local/bin/codex-bridge" ``` **Intel / amd64** ```sh curl -fL https://github.com/agent0ai/codex-bridge/releases/latest/download/codex-bridge-darwin-amd64 -o codex-bridge-darwin-amd64 && mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin" && install -m 755 codex-bridge-darwin-amd64 "$HOME/.local/bin/codex-bridge" ``` ### PATH If `~/.local/bin` is not already on PATH, add it for this shell and put the same line in `~/.zshrc` (macOS's default Zsh) or `~/.bashrc` (Bash) for future terminals: ```sh export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" ``` [Config](config.example.yaml) · [Guide](docs/guide.md) · [MIT License](LICENSE) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [Third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) ---

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Live image and local-file checks. Requires a0-vision, a0-qwen and a ChatGPT login."""
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import struct
import subprocess
import tempfile
import zlib


def png(path, left, right):
    width, height = 160, 80
    raw = b"".join(b"\0" + b"".join(bytes(left if x < width // 2 else right)
                                  for x in range(width)) for _ in range(height))

    def chunk(kind, data):
        return (struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + kind + data
                + struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(kind + data) & 0xffffffff))

    path.write_bytes(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"
                     + chunk(b"IHDR", struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", width, height, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0))
                     + chunk(b"IDAT", zlib.compress(raw)) + chunk(b"IEND", b""))


def run(cwd, model, prompt, images=None, resume=None):
    command = ["codex", "exec"]
    if resume:
        command += ["resume", resume]
    command += ["--skip-git-repo-check", "--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox",
                "-m", model, "--json"]
    if images:
        command += ["--image", ",".join(images)]
    result = subprocess.run(command + ["--", prompt], cwd=cwd, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=180)
    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stdout + result.stderr
    events = [json.loads(line) for line in result.stdout.splitlines()]
    assert any(e["type"] == "turn.completed" for e in events), events
    messages = [e["item"]["text"] for e in events if e["type"] == "item.completed"
                and e["item"]["type"] == "agent_message"]
    thread_id = next(e["thread_id"] for e in events if e["type"] == "thread.started")
    return "\n".join(messages).lower(), thread_id, events


with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="bridge-attachments-") as directory:
    root = Path(directory)
    png(root / "a.png", (255, 0, 0), (0, 0, 255))
    png(root / "b.png", (0, 180, 0), (255, 255, 0))
    (root / "note.txt").write_text("Marker: COBALT-482\nCount: 37\n")

    text, thread, _ = run(root, "a0-vision", "Name the image's two colors from left to right. Do not use tools.", ["a.png"])
    assert "red" in text and "blue" in text and text.index("red") < text.index("blue"), text
    print("PASS single PNG attachment", flush=True)
    for model in ("gpt-6-luna", "a0-vision"):
        text, _, _ = run(root, model, "What were the two colors in the image I attached? Give left-to-right order. Do not use tools.", resume=thread)
        assert "red" in text and "blue" in text, (model, text)
        print(f"PASS image history retained when switching to {model}", flush=True)

    text, _, _ = run(root, "a0-vision", "For image 1 and image 2, report the two colors in left-to-right order. Do not use tools.", ["a.png", "b.png"])
    positions = [text.index(color) for color in ("red", "blue", "green", "yellow")]
    assert positions == sorted(positions), text
    print("PASS multiple PNG attachments in order", flush=True)

    text, thread, _ = run(root, "a0-vision", "Use view_image to open b.png and report its colors left to right. Do not inspect image bytes with shell or Python.")
    assert "green" in text and "yellow" in text, text
    sessions = Path(os.environ.get("CODEX_HOME", str(Path.home() / ".codex"))) / "sessions"
    paths = list(sessions.rglob(f"*{thread}.jsonl"))
    assert paths, thread
    payloads = [json.loads(line).get("payload", {}) for line in paths[0].read_text().splitlines()]
    assert any(p.get("type") == "function_call" and p.get("name") == "view_image" for p in payloads)
    print("PASS view_image tool output reaches the vision model", flush=True)

    text, _, events = run(root, "a0-qwen", "Read @note.txt with a file-reading tool and report its marker and count.")
    assert "cobalt-482" in text and "37" in text, text
    assert any(e.get("item", {}).get("type") == "command_execution" for e in events), events
    print("PASS local text-file reference read through Codex tools", flush=True)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Live Codex model-switch test; uses paid API calls. Run inside the test container."""
import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path
import queue
import secrets
import subprocess
import tempfile
import threading

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--external-only", action="store_true")
parser.add_argument("--subscription-model", default="gpt-6-luna")
args = parser.parse_args()
command = ["codex", "app-server", "--listen", "stdio://"]
if args.external_only:
    command += ["-c", "model_providers.codex-bridge.requires_openai_auth=false"]

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="bridge-smoke-") as cwd, tempfile.TemporaryFile() as stderr:
    process = subprocess.Popen(command, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                               stderr=stderr, text=True)
    inbox = queue.Queue()

    def read():
        for line in process.stdout:
            inbox.put(json.loads(line))
        inbox.put({"error": "app-server exited"})

    threading.Thread(target=read, daemon=True).start()
    sequence = 0
    notifications = []

    def send(message):
        process.stdin.write(json.dumps(message) + "\n")
        process.stdin.flush()

    def request(method, params):
        global sequence
        sequence += 1
        send({"id": sequence, "method": method, "params": params})
        while True:
            message = inbox.get(timeout=180)
            if "error" in message:
                raise RuntimeError(message["error"])
            if message.get("id") == sequence:
                return message["result"]
            notifications.append(message)

    try:
        request("initialize", {"clientInfo": {"name": "bridge_smoke", "version": "0.1.0"},
                               "capabilities": {"experimentalApi": True}})
        send({"method": "initialized"})
        models = request("model/list", {"includeHidden": False, "limit": 100})["data"]
        names = [model["model"] for model in models]
        assert "a0-qwen" in names and "a0-deepseek" in names, names
        assert args.subscription_model in names, names
        print("Model picker includes external and subscription models", flush=True)
        result = request("thread/start", {"cwd": cwd, "model": "a0-qwen",
                         "modelProvider": "codex-bridge", "approvalPolicy": "never",
                         "sandbox": "danger-full-access"})
        thread_id = result["thread"]["id"]
        plan = [("a0-qwen", "Use apply_patch to create marker.txt containing ORBIT-731. Remember this marker and reply with it."),
                ("a0-deepseek", "Read marker.txt using a shell tool, then reply with the marker I gave you.")]
        if not args.external_only:
            plan.append((args.subscription_model, "Read marker.txt using a tool, then reply with the marker I gave you."))
        plan.append(("a0-qwen", "Read marker.txt using a shell tool, then reply with the marker I gave you."))
        for model, prompt in plan:
            probe = None
            if (Path(cwd) / "marker.txt").exists():
                probe = "PROBE-" + secrets.token_hex(4)
                (Path(cwd) / "probe.txt").write_text(probe + "\n")
                prompt += " Also read probe.txt using a tool now and include its exact contents; it has a new value unavailable in conversation history."
            notifications.clear()
            request("turn/start", {"threadId": thread_id, "model": model,
                                  "input": [{"type": "text", "text": prompt}]})
            text = ""
            tool_count = 0
            while True:
                message = notifications.pop(0) if notifications else inbox.get(timeout=180)
                if "error" in message:
                    raise RuntimeError(message["error"])
                if message.get("method") == "item/agentMessage/delta":
                    text += message["params"]["delta"]
                if message.get("method") == "item/completed" and message["params"]["item"]["type"] in ("commandExecution", "fileChange"):
                    tool_count += 1
                if message.get("method") == "turn/completed":
                    turn = message["params"]["turn"]
                    assert turn["status"] == "completed", turn
                    break
            assert "ORBIT-731" in text, (model, text)
            if probe:
                assert probe in text, (model, "fresh file value missing", text)
            assert (Path(cwd) / "marker.txt").read_text().strip() == "ORBIT-731"
            assert tool_count > 0, (model, "no completed file or command tool")
            print(f"PASS {model}: same thread {thread_id}, marker preserved, {tool_count} completed tools", flush=True)
        print("PASS model switching without profiles", flush=True)
    finally:
        process.terminate()
        try:
            process.wait(timeout=10)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            process.kill()
            process.wait(timeout=10)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Native lifecycle and TUI regression: stale catalog, --no-daemon, sync --force.

Uses a temporary CODEX_HOME, dummy credentials, and no inference requests.
Requires Linux/macOS and a complete Codex 0.164.0 installation for daemon start.
"""

def picker(env, cwd, flags=()):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", 45, 160, 0, 0))
    process = subprocess.Popen(["codex", "--no-alt-screen", *flags], env=env, cwd=cwd,
                               stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, start_new_session=True)
    os.close(slave)

    def read_until(*needles, timeout=40):
        output = b""
        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            if select.select([master], [], [], 0.1)[0]:
                chunk = os.read(master, 65536)
                output += chunk
                if b"\x1b[6n" in chunk:
                    os.write(master, b"\x1b[1;1R")
                clean = re.sub(rb"\x1b\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~]", b"", output)
                if all(needle in clean for needle in needles):
                    return clean.decode(errors="replace")
            if process.poll() is not None:
                break
        raise AssertionError(f"TUI did not show {needles!r}: {output[-5000:]!r}")

    try:
        read_until(b"state=idle")
        os.write(master, b"/model")
        time.sleep(0.3)
        os.write(master, b"\r")
        return read_until(b"Select Model and Effort", b"esc back")
    finally:
        os.write(master, b"\x1b\x03\x03")
        try:
            process.wait(timeout=8)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            process.kill()
            process.wait(timeout=5)
        os.close(master)

        lines = [line for line in result.stdout.splitlines() if line.startswith("Codex sync:")]

        print("PASS live status: " + expected, flush=True)

    print(run("codex", "--version").strip(), flush=True)
    run(args.bridge, "edit")
    assert bridge_config.read_text().endswith("# edited\n"), "edit missed the default config path"
    print("PASS default config and editor argument with spaces: " + str(bridge_config), flush=True)

    try:

        result = run(args.bridge, "--config", str(bridge_config), "restart")

            assert result.returncode != 0, result.stdout
            bridge_config.write_text(working_config)
            assert "Already running" in run(args.bridge, "start"), "invalid restart stopped the working proxy"
        print("PASS restart while stopped/running, port change, and invalid config/key preservation", flush=True)
        run("codex", "app-server", "daemon", "start")
        run(args.bridge, "--config", str(bridge_config), "sync")
        verify_status("unsynced")
        stale = picker(env, cwd)
        assert "Select Model and Effort" in stale and "picker-test-model" not in stale, stale
        print("PASS real TUI reproduces the stale catalog after normal sync", flush=True)
        fresh = picker(env, cwd, ["--no-daemon"])
        assert "1. picker-test-model" in fresh, fresh
        print("PASS --no-daemon shows the external model first", flush=True)
        run(args.bridge, "--config", str(bridge_config), "sync", "--force")
        verify_status("synced")
        restarted = picker(env, cwd)
        assert "1. picker-test-model" in restarted, restarted
        print("PASS sync --force refreshes the normal shared-server TUI picker", flush=True)
        bridge_config.write_text(bridge_config.read_text() + "    vision: true\n")
        run(args.bridge, "--config", str(bridge_config), "sync")
        verify_status("unsynced")
        run(args.bridge, "--config", str(bridge_config), "sync", "--force")
        verify_status("synced")
        run("codex", "app-server", "daemon", "stop")
        verify_status("could not verify")
    finally:

        finally:
            run(args.bridge, "stop")
    stopped = subprocess.run([args.bridge, "status"], env=env, cwd=cwd,
                             capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=20)
    assert stopped.returncode != 0 and "Stopped or unreachable" in stopped.stdout, (stopped.stdout, stopped.stderr)

# codex-bridge

A small Go proxy that puts OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions and Responses models in Codex CLI's `/model` picker, alongside your ChatGPT subscription. Switch models within a conversation; no profiles or patched Codex required.

Proof of concept using **Codex CLI 0.164.0**. Live inference was tested on Debian Linux; macOS verification covers native lifecycle and the Codex picker without inference (see [verification](../verification.txt)). YAML and TOML parsers plus a WebSocket client for checking Codex's loaded models; no database or JavaScript runtime for the proxy. The running proxy used about 15 MiB RSS during the initial Linux live tests. Windows support is not implemented.

## Ready-to-use test container

The running container is `codex-bridge-lab`. It has Codex, the bridge, three external models, and your subscription login. The disposable provider key is stored only in its private bridge config, not in this repository or image.

```bash
docker exec -it codex-bridge-lab bash
codex-bridge status
cd /work
codex --no-daemon
```

Inside Codex, enter `/model` and select `a0-qwen`, `a0-deepseek`, `a0-vision`, or a subscription model such as `GPT-6-Luna`. External models appear first, in config order. To start with a specific external model, use `codex --no-daemon -m a0-qwen`.

```bash
codex-bridge edit       # $VISUAL, then $EDITOR, then automatic editor detection
codex-bridge sync       # validate config and write the model catalog
codex --no-daemon       # load the current config without using the shared server
# Or, to use normal codex (this may interrupt active shared-server work):
codex-bridge sync --force
codex
codex-bridge restart
```

Routing and body parameter changes are loaded on the next request. The bridge caches native model IDs and reloads the installed Codex catalog when a requested model is missing, so newly installed models work without restarting the proxy. Native OpenAI HTTP errors and connection failures clear the cache for the next request; failed inference requests are not replayed by the bridge. Unknown models are still rejected; a catalog read failure returns a retryable error. External requests do not read the Codex catalog. Run `codex-bridge restart` after changing the listen address, inherited environment variables, or the bridge binary. `stop` and `status` still work if you make a config syntax error or change the configured port.

## Install on your own machine

Install Codex CLI 0.164.0 and Go 1.24.4 or newer, then run in a source checkout on Linux or macOS (see the [README](../README.md) for downloads and cloning):

```bash
go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w -X main.version=$(git describe --tags --always --dirty)" -o codex-bridge . &&
mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin" &&
install -m 755 codex-bridge "$HOME/.local/bin/codex-bridge"
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
codex-bridge edit       # creates the initial config if missing
```

If needed, put the `export PATH` line in `~/.bashrc` (Bash) or `~/.zshrc` (Zsh, the macOS default) for future terminals. The default config is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/codex-bridge/config.yaml` on Linux (normally `~/.config/codex-bridge/config.yaml`), and `~/Library/Application Support/codex-bridge/config.yaml` on macOS. The proxy also supports an explicit file; quote paths with spaces, for example `codex-bridge --config "$HOME/Library/Application Support/codex-bridge/config.yaml" start`. Legacy `.toml` files remain readable when passed explicitly with `--config`. Codex's own `~/.codex/config.toml` still uses TOML.

`codex-bridge --version` prints the binary's build version without requiring a config. `status` also shows this version. Release builds embed their Git tag; builds without `-X main.version=...` report `dev`.

`init` creates the example config; `edit` automatically does this when the file is missing, then opens it. Existing configs are preserved, including invalid configs that need fixing. `start` and `sync` require an existing config and never create one automatically.

`edit` honors `$VISUAL`, then `$EDITOR`. With neither set, it searches `PATH` in this order: `micro`, `nano`, `mcedit`, `joe`, `nvim`, `vim`, the system `editor` command, then `vi`. The first available executable is used. An explicit editor setting that fails produces an error rather than silently switching editors. If no editor is found or the selected editor fails, the error includes the full config path so you can edit it manually.

The initial config contains Venice DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (`deepseek-v4-1-flash`) under the alias `a0-deepseek`, with the tested reasoning parameter fix. Replace `api_key: "..."` with your key. To use an environment variable instead, comment out `api_key`, uncomment `api_key_env: AGENT_ZERO_API_KEY`, and export that variable **before starting the proxy**:

```bash
read -rs -p 'Provider API key: ' AGENT_ZERO_API_KEY; echo
export AGENT_ZERO_API_KEY
```

Then start and sync:

```bash
codex-bridge start
codex-bridge sync
codex login             # only if you have not already logged in
codex --no-daemon
```

The bridge uses Codex's existing subscription authentication and refresh logic. It never modifies `auth.json` or logs credentials. A subscription login is required for the normal mixed subscription/external setup. For external-only use without signing in, launch `codex -c model_providers.codex-bridge.requires_openai_auth=false -m a0-deepseek`.

## Config

See [config.example.yaml](../config.example.yaml) for the initial DeepSeek V4.1 Flash config. The existing test container keeps its separate three-model config for the Qwen, DeepSeek, and vision tests. A model entry looks like:

```yaml
listen: 127.0.0.1:8787
models:
  - name: my-model                       # unique name in Codex's picker
    model: actual-provider-model-id      # defaults to name
    base_url: https://provider.example/v1
    api: chat                            # chat or responses
    api_key_env: MY_PROVIDER_KEY          # or api_key: "literal key"
    context_window: 131072                # defaults to 32768
    vision: false                        # true for image-capable models
    reasoning_efforts: [low, high]        # omit if unsupported
    drop_params: [parallel_tool_calls]   # omit parameters the provider rejects
    params:
      temperature: 0.2
      max_tokens: 8192
      vendor_options:
        thinking: true
```

`params` accepts JSON-compatible YAML values and recursively merges them into the upstream JSON body after translation. Unknown config fields, duplicate keys, multiple YAML documents, and parameters with non-string map keys are rejected. `drop_params` removes top-level fields first. Routing and protocol fields (`model`, `input`, `messages`, `tools`, `stream`) are controlled by the bridge. Credentials use a Bearer token; omit both key settings for an unauthenticated local API. URLs may include an arbitrary path and query parameters, and may point to the API base or complete endpoint.

Changing `context_window` does not enlarge the provider's real context limit. Set it to a value the model actually supports. An API-compatible model still needs good tool-call support to perform coding tasks reliably.

## Commands and configuration safety

| Command | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `init` | Create the example config with private permissions; never overwrite an existing file. |
| `edit` | Create the example config if missing, then open it with your terminal editor. |
| `sync` | Validate config, generate a version-matched model catalog, and select the local bridge provider. |
| `sync --force` | Sync, then immediately invoke `codex app-server daemon restart`; active work may be interrupted. |
| `start` | Start one background proxy; repeated starts reuse the running instance. |
| `stop` | Stop the listener and allow active requests up to ten seconds to finish. |
| `restart` | Gracefully stop the proxy, then start with the current config and environment; also starts a stopped proxy. |
| `status` | Show proxy health, configured model count, and whether Codex's provider/catalog match the bridge. |
| `serve` | Run in the foreground; stop with Ctrl-C. |
| `unsync` | Restore the prior provider/catalog settings while preserving unrelated config changes. |

`sync` writes `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml` and `codex-bridge-models.json` (normally under `~/.codex`). It preserves unrelated settings and comments, creates `config.toml.bridge-backup`, and is idempotent. It refuses to overwrite an existing unmanaged `codex-bridge` provider or a separate custom model catalog. Profiles are never created. Model aliases must not collide with built-in model names.

After updating Codex, run `sync` to refresh the picker catalog. The bridge refreshes its model-ID cache on a missing model or after a native upstream error, but Codex's picker still needs to load the synced file. `restart` restarts only the bridge proxy; `sync --force` restarts Codex's shared server. Invalid config or missing environment-based API keys abort `restart` before stopping a working proxy.

Codex 0.164.0 can reconnect new terminals to an existing shared background server. That server keeps its startup model catalog, so **closing and reopening the terminal does not refresh it**. Use `codex --no-daemon` to load the synced files immediately, or run `codex-bridge sync --force` and reopen Codex. The force option restarts the shared server through Codex's own daemon command, which may interrupt active work and takes time to shut down gracefully. Normal `sync` never restarts it. If restarting fails, the command exits with an error and clearly reports that the files were still synced.

`status` verifies the provider, local token, listen address, and model catalog files, then connects to the **running** Codex server's Unix socket and queries its [`model/list` API](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server#list-models-modellist). It checks external model names, order, visibility, descriptions, reasoning options, and input modalities, including removed models still loaded by the server. It reports one result: `synced`, `unsynced`, or `could not verify`. A stopped/unreachable server, failed query, or malformed response produces `could not verify`; a confirmed difference produces `unsynced`. Reasons appear only when verification fails or finds a mismatch.

The query is read-only: it does not start/restart Codex or send inference requests. It follows pagination and has a ten-second deadline for the server check. Changing API keys or upstream parameters does not require sync; changing model metadata does. The API exposes picker metadata, not all internal settings such as retained context limits or provider credentials. Separate profiles, command-line overrides, and upstream model access are outside this check.

```text
Version: v0.1.1
Running at http://127.0.0.1:8787
Config: /root/.config/codex-bridge/config.yaml
Models: 1 external
Codex sync: synced
Codex config: /root/.codex/config.toml
```

All selected models go through the proxy while synced, so keep it running. To return to your original setup:

```bash
codex-bridge unsync
codex-bridge stop
# Use codex --no-daemon, or restart the shared server and reopen Codex.
# If you last selected an external alias, choose a built-in model.
```

The proxy binds only to a loopback IP and requires a random local token written by `sync`. Browser-origin requests are rejected. Third-party requests are built with only that model's credentials; subscription headers are sent only to fixed OpenAI destinations. HTTP redirects are not followed for third-party requests. Logs contain model, status, and timing rather than prompts or keys. The log is next to the config as `config.yaml.log`.

## Translation and limits

Supported: streamed text, multiple tool calls, tool results and multi-turn history, namespaced tools, custom/freeform tools (including `apply_patch`), reasoning summaries and replay, image URLs/data URLs, inline file data, structured-output schemas, usage counts, token-limit endings, upstream errors, cancellation, and native Responses forwarding. Summary-only reasoning is converted to text when crossing into Responses so OpenAI does not attempt to retrieve invented server-side item IDs.

This is a Codex-focused adapter, not a complete implementation of every Responses API feature:

- Chat Completions has no hosted OpenAI web search. The bridge removes that tool and tells the model it is unavailable. Use an MCP search tool or provider-specific `params`. Subscription web search remains intact.
- Audio, video, uploaded file IDs/URLs, computer-use tools, background jobs, and `previous_response_id` storage are not emulated for Chat Completions. Unsupported inputs fail explicitly. Codex's HTTP mode sends complete history and works without a response database.
- Encrypted OpenAI reasoning cannot be converted to another provider's private reasoning format. Available summaries and visible conversation/tool history are preserved.
- Tool arguments are buffered until complete and validated before execution. Truncated or malformed calls produce an error rather than executing a partial command.
- Native subscription capabilities, eligibility, and rate limits still apply. The bundled model catalog includes models your account might not have. GPT-6.1-Sol reported capacity errors during the live tests; GPT-6-Luna completed the mixed-provider test.
- Switching models does not raise the destination model's context limit. Large or unusual provider-specific conversations need further testing. Do not assume every provider-specific extension is interchangeable.

## Images and files

Use an image-capable model with `vision = true`:

```bash
codex -m a0-vision --image screenshot.png -- 'Describe this screenshot.'
codex -m a0-qwen 'Read @notes.txt and summarize it.'
```

Live checks passed for a single PNG, two PNGs in order, `view_image` tool output, a local text-file reference read through Codex tools, and retaining an image when switching external → subscription → external. Image/file media returned by tools is placed after all parallel tool results, because Chat tool messages accept only text. Inline Responses `input_file.file_data` maps to Chat's file content part; the destination must support that file type. This mapping has fixture coverage; PDF interpretation was not tested live.

## Prompt caching

The bridge preserves `prompt_cache_key`, `prompt_cache_retention`, `prompt_cache_options`, and content-part cache controls. It generates stable tool aliases and deterministic JSON, without inserting a new timestamp or random value into the upstream prompt on every request. Regression tests check that identical input produces identical output and adding a turn preserves the earlier message prefix.

The live test captured each upstream `usage` object during four consecutive turns in one Codex thread per model:

| Model | Turn | Input tokens | Cached input | Hit ratio |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen Coder | 1 | 74,666 | 0 | 0% |
| Qwen Coder | 2 | 74,697 | 74,640 | 99.92% |
| Qwen Coder | 3 | 74,728 | 74,672 | 99.93% |
| Qwen Coder | 4 | 74,759 | 74,704 | 99.93% |
| DeepSeek V3.2 | 1 | 68,518 | 0 | 0% |
| DeepSeek V3.2 | 2 | 68,544 | 68,416 | 99.81% |
| DeepSeek V3.2 | 3 | 68,570 | 68,416 | 99.78% |
| DeepSeek V3.2 | 4 | 68,596 | 68,480 | 99.83% |

Hit ratio is `cached_input_tokens / input_tokens`. Follow-up turns had weighted hit ratios of **99.93% for Qwen** and **99.81% for DeepSeek**; a final Qwen rerun measured **99.92%**. Every earlier message, tool definition, and cache key stayed unchanged across those requests. The script uses a private proxy and an in-memory upstream tap; reports contain usage counters, not prompts or credentials. These were short answers to a fixed reference prompt, without tool execution in the cache measurement itself; tool execution is covered separately by the smoke tests.

Standard `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` maps to Responses `input_tokens_details.cached_tokens`; DeepSeek's `prompt_cache_hit_tokens` is a fallback. Input/output detail fields are retained. Codex CLI reports cumulative thread usage after `exec resume`, so the test subtracts the previous total and checks that input, cached input, and output counts exactly match the upstream turn. See [cache-verification.json](../cache-verification.json) for the original usage objects and verified deltas.

The supplied gateway replaces `prompt_cache_key` with its own stable account key. Preserving Codex's key fixes a portability issue for other providers, even though that gateway already supplied one. A later YAML-config verification run measured 36.28% weighted follow-up reuse, with an unchanged prefix and exact usage accounting; its raw usage is also in the report. Cache availability, retention, routing, model changes, compaction, and real prompt changes still affect reuse; these measurements do not guarantee a particular hit ratio for other workloads.

## Verification and reproducible Docker image

```bash
go test -race ./...
go vet ./...
# Real terminal picker regression; isolated daemon, dummy key, no model requests:
python3 tests/picker.py
docker build --build-arg VERSION="$(git describe --tags --always --dirty)" -t codex-bridge:proof .
docker run -d --name my-codex-bridge --init codex-bridge:proof
docker exec -it my-codex-bridge bash
# Run init/edit/start/sync and codex login inside this new container.
```

No ports need publishing: Codex and the proxy share the container's loopback interface. This image uses Debian slim, a static Go bridge, the native Codex binary, Node for Codex's JavaScript tool, and basic coding tools. The image contains no credentials. Keep or back up the container's home directory before removing it.

## GitHub releases

The [build/release workflow](../.github/workflows/release.yml) verifies branch pushes without publishing. A stable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` tag additionally publishes a release after all four native Linux/macOS amd64/arm64 jobs pass tests and build binaries with CGO disabled. The Mac jobs also run the isolated lifecycle and real Codex picker regression. The prepared release assets are `codex-bridge-linux-amd64`, `codex-bridge-linux-arm64`, `codex-bridge-darwin-amd64` (Intel), `codex-bridge-darwin-arm64` (Apple Silicon), `checksums.txt` covering all four, the MIT license, and third-party notices.

Release notes include commits since the previous stable tag. Assets are uploaded to a draft before publication; retries can complete a draft but cannot overwrite a published release. Older version tags do not replace the latest release used by the README's download links. The workflow uses GitHub's job token and needs no custom release secrets. Mac binaries have not yet been published; use the README's source build until a release containing those assets exists.

## Live provider checks

The live smoke test makes real provider requests and creates a temporary marker file using Codex tools. The cache script uses PyYAML, included in the image (`apt install python3-yaml` when running it separately on Debian):

```bash
docker exec codex-bridge-lab python3 /opt/bridge-smoke.py
# Or without a subscription login:
docker exec codex-bridge-lab python3 /opt/bridge-smoke.py --external-only
# Image/file checks, including subscription model switching:
docker exec codex-bridge-lab python3 /opt/bridge-attachments.py
# Four-turn cache checks with raw usage reports:
docker exec codex-bridge-lab python3 /opt/bridge-cache.py --model a0-qwen --report /tmp/cache-qwen.json
docker exec codex-bridge-lab python3 /opt/bridge-cache.py --model a0-deepseek --report /tmp/cache-deepseek.json
```

The picker regression requires a complete packaged Codex 0.164.0 installation for daemon management; pass `--codex /path/to/package/bin/codex` if your default CLI is a standalone binary, and `--bridge /path/to/codex-bridge` to test a build. It checks the default config path with spaces, editor invocation, background start/repeated start/stop, and status. It reproduces a stale catalog after normal sync, checks `--no-daemon`, then checks that `sync --force` makes the external model appear first in a normal terminal session. It also checks live status before/after restart, stale image support for an existing alias, and the stopped-server result. It gives subprocesses a temporary home and `CODEX_HOME`, dummy credentials, and an offline provider; existing configs and servers are untouched.

Unit tests cover translation, fragmented parallel tool calls, custom tools, reasoning, attachments, cache controls and accounting, stable prompt prefixes, JSON schemas, truncated streams, credential separation, native Responses forwarding, URL handling, validation, sync/unsync preservation, force restart, and restart failures. Live tests cover Qwen file edits and Python tests, DeepSeek reasoning and shell tools, image and file attachments, cache reuse, the interactive picker, and switching external/subscription models within one thread. See [verification.txt](../verification.txt) for the recorded results.

Implementation references: [Codex configuration](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference), [Codex v0.164.0 source](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/rust-v0.164.0), and [MetaFARS/codex-relay](https://github.com/MetaFARS/codex-relay) (translation edge cases).
